question.problem:
| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.5$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.2$ |

Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{50}$ be a random sample of size $n=50$ from a population with the probability mass function given above. Find an approximation for the probability that the sample mean is greater than $2.2.$

*Note: $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is 

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =50,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}f({x}_{i}) \\  & =1\cdot 0.5+2\cdot 0.2+3\cdot 0.1+4\cdot 0.2 \\  & =0.5+0.4+0.3+0.8 \\  & =2,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\text{Var}[X] \\  & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =({1}^{2}\cdot 0.5+{2}^{2}\cdot 0.2+{3}^{2}\cdot 0.1+{4}^{2}\cdot 0.2)-{2}^{2} \\  & =(0.5+0.8+0.9+3.2)-4 \\  & =1.4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(2,\frac{1.4}{50}) \\  & ∼N(2,0.028).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(\overset{―}{X}>2.2).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(\overset{―}{X}>2.2) & ≈P(Z>\frac{2.2-2}{\sqrt{0.028}}) \\  & =P(Z>1.20) \\  & =1-Φ(1.20).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
P(\overset{―}{X}>2.2)=1-Φ(1.20).
$$
